record.original_question: Suppose that |zk | = 1 (1 ≤ k < ∞). Put m X Al = lim sup zkl . m→∞ k=1 It is easy to see that there is a sequence zk , for which Al < cl for all l, and Clunie [160] proved Al > cl 2 for infinitely many l. Is there a sequence for which Al = o(l) as l → ∞? (P. Erdös)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(z_k)_{k=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of complex numbers with $|z_k|=1$ for every $k\ge 1$. For each positive integer $l$, define
$$A_l \;=\; \limsup_{m\to\infty}\,\Bigl|\sum_{k=1}^{m} z_k^{\,l}\Bigr|.$$
It is known that there exist sequences $(z_k)$ for which $A_l < c\,l$ for all $l$ (with some absolute constant $c>0$), and it has been proved that for every such sequence one has $A_l > c\,l^{1/2}$ for infinitely many $l$.

Question: Does there exist a sequence $(z_k)_{k\ge 1}$ on the unit circle such that
$$A_l = o(l) \qquad \text{as } l \to \infty\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive resolution of this particular Erdős question on the growth of $A_l = \limsup_m |\sum_{k\le m} z_k^l|$ for unimodular sequences. Recent related work (e.g., a 2025 result that the sequence of partial sums of a unimodular power series cannot be ultraflat) addresses adjacent questions but does not appear to settle whether some unimodular sequence achieves $A_l = o(l)$. The status of this specific problem could not be confirmed from available sources.

status_evidence.title: The sequence of partial sums of a unimodular power series is not ultraflat
status_evidence.snippet: If (a_j) has |a_j|=1 and P_n(z)=sum a_j z^j, then (P_n) is not an ultraflat sequence of unimodular polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: A related result on partial sums of unimodular sequences from 2025, but it does not directly resolve the o(l) question for A_l.
